subject: DPA/SCCs: role ownership and cross-border routing questions
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@procureco.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@procureco.com; marco.ruiz@procureco.com
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood MSA / DPA redlines and SCCs questions

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for sending over the MSA and order form. We ran the draft by LegalOps and have a few focused questions on the DPA and SCCs before we can move to procurement signature. To keep the review tight, our three main asks:

1) Role ownership: your DPA lists Redwood as "processor" for model inference logs; however, our data protection team expects the service provider to be controller for derived operational metadata. Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept the processor role across the mosaic of telemetry and inference artifacts, or whether you expect ProcureCo to retain controller status for certain outputs? If the latter, we need suggested clause language to clarify.

2) SCCs module: we use EU data for a UK/US hybrid deployment. Please confirm which SCCs variant Redwood intends to adopt (EU Standard Clauses module 2/3/4). Also confirm any proposed Addendum for UK transfers.

3) Transfer-impact addendum / export controls: our security team wants a short transfer-impact note that maps which regions (US, EU, APAC) are used for model hosting and whether key management is customer or Redwood-managed.

I've attached our redlines to the MSA (ProcureCo_MSA_redlines_20280309.pdf) and put a short CSV mapping in the drive (link below). Can your team propose wording for the role ownership point and share an annotated DPA showing the agreed SCCs module?

Proposed timeline: we plan to get legal sign-off by 2028-03-21 if the remaining items are small.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to hop on a 30 minute call next week if easier.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Senior Contracts Manager | ProcureCo
attachments: ProcureCo_MSA_redlines_20280309.pdf

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@procureco.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA / DPA redlines and SCCs questions

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in Ben (sales lead on the deal) and Irene (privacy counsel) so we can answer with one proposal.

Quick answers up front:
- Role ownership: Redwood's standard position is processor for customer content and detector telemetry; we are willing to accept processor role for inference inputs/outputs and operational logs. Where customers retain controller status for aggregated analytics or derived models, we can add clarifying language that Redwood will act as a processor except where Customer explicitly indicates controller intent for specific data types. Irene will propose precise clause wording.
- SCCs: Redwood supports EU SCCs (module 2) and will provide a UK Addendum. We typically map to the SCCs module that aligns with the data flow; happy to confirm module selection after we validate your regional hosting map.
- KMS/hosting: Redwood can support customer-managed keys (BYOK) in Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted customers keys are Redwood-managed by default but we can offer a KMS integration note in the DPA.

We'll prepare an annotated DPA and a short transfer-impact addendum draft. Expect a first pass from us on Monday 2028-03-12. If ProcureCo is available, let's schedule a 30-minute call on Tue 3/13 or Wed 3/14 to iron out role language and the SCCs module selection.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@procureco.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@procureco.com>, contracts@procureco.com
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 07:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood MSA / DPA redlines and SCCs questions

Thanks Lauren — Tue 3/13 09:00 PT works for us. A couple of clarifications in advance so your annotated DPA can target our needs:

- We host a subset of EU personal data for product telemetry tied to EU customers; that dataset must remain under EU SCCs and should not be routable to non-EU regions except for operational troubleshooting. Can you confirm technical routing controls to ensure this?
- On role ownership: we can accept controller-for-derived-analytics language but need sample wording that limits assignment to clearly enumerated categories (e.g., aggregated usage metrics, model improvements based on customer opt-in).

We'll be on the call with our Privacy Ops and Infra lead to confirm the routing map.

—Marco
Director, Procurement | ProcureCo

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@procureco.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@procureco.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood MSA / DPA redlines and SCCs questions

Hi Emma / Marco — thanks for the extra detail. Attached is an annotated DPA (Redwood_DPA_annotated_20280310.docx) and a short transfer-impact spreadsheet (SCCs-transfer-impact-notes.xlsx) that maps likely processing locations by dataset category. Key points from our side:

1) Processor/controller split (proposed clause):
"Redwood shall act as Processor with respect to Customer Personal Data submitted to the Service for inference and supporting logs. For clarity, where Customer separately designates specific derived datasets or aggregated analytics as Controller data in writing, the parties will document such designation in Appendix X and Redwood's processing shall be limited to the scope expressly set forth therein."

This preserves your right to retain controller status for narrowly defined derived artifacts while keeping Redwood as processor for the core service. Please review and confirm whether the examples in Appendix X are sufficient; we can expand the list live on the call.

2) SCCs / UK Addendum: we recommend Module 2 SCCs for controller-to-processor transfers and will include a UK Addendum. For customer-data that must stay within EU, we propose a routing SLA: Redwood will not route identified EU-customer personal data outside EU boundary regions except for (a) emergency troubleshooting with logged temporary access, or (b) where Customer consents in writing. We included sample SLA text in the spreadsheet.

3) Key management: by default Hosted customers will have Redwood-managed keys; we have optional BYOK integrations for Dedicated and Private customers and will list the KMS options in Appendix Y. If ProcureCo requires BYOK for Hosted, we can scope that as a Professional Services add-on (ops & timeline note included).

Next steps: 1) confirm the example list for Appendix X; 2) confirm whether the EU-exception carveout language is acceptable; 3) run the attached DPA by your Privacy Ops before the call.

Proposed call: Tue 2028-03-13 09:00 PT — dial-in link in calendar invite.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_DPA_annotated_20280310.docx; SCCs-transfer-impact-notes.xlsx

Subject: RE: Redwood MSA / DPA redlines and SCCs questions — post-call notes and next steps

Great discussion today — appreciate everyone making time. Short summary and actions:

Summary:
- Parties aligned on processor role for inference inputs/outputs and operational logs; ProcureCo will retain controller status for any derived analytics they explicitly designate in Appendix X.
- Redwood to adopt EU SCCs (Module 2) for the Controller->Processor path and provide UK Addendum draft.
- For EU-only datasets, Redwood will implement routing controls and a temporary emergency access protocol; details in SCCs-transfer-impact-notes.xlsx.
- BYOK: ProcureCo prefers customer-managed keys for production; Redwood will scope BYOK for Hosted as a PS deliverable (estimate: 4-6 weeks after order form execution).

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Irene: finalize proposed Appendix X clause and add example list (ETA: 2028-03-16).
- Lauren: update order form to reflect the BYOK PS line item and note in the commercial summary (ETA: 2028-03-15).
- Ben: attach final commercial snapshot and send an updated order form template for signatures after legal confirmation (ETA: 2028-03-17).
- Emma / Marco: review the annotated DPA and Appendix X examples, confirm routing map (ETA: 2028-03-18).

I've attached the call notes and will follow up with the updated order form and PS estimate. If anything above is inaccurate, flag it here and we'll correct. Otherwise, we'll move towards signature once Appendix X is agreed.

Best,
Ben Carter
